title: \(2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}\) lower bound for binary edit distance in \(\ell_1\)
formal:
For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\) be the infimum distortion of embeddings of all length-\(n\) binary strings, with unit-cost edit distance, into finite-dimensional \(\ell_1\). Distortion measures the worst multiplicative change in any distance after a common rescaling; its precise all-pairs definition is below.

Do there exist an absolute real constant \(c>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge2\) such that
\[
D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\ge 2^{c\sqrt{\log_2 n}}
\qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge n_0?
\]
This is the assertion that binary edit distance requires \(\ell_1\) distortion at least \(2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}\).
